title: 3-D Secure
applicability: Conditional 3-D Secure material for eCommerce authorization messages involving Visa Verified by Visa, MasterCard SecureCode/Identity Check, or American Express SafeKey. Appendix Y also names Discover in its general 3-D Secure discussion, but supplies no Discover cryptogram mapping.
source: specifications/ATL105/docs/specs/extracted_text.txt Appendix Y-1 through Y-3; related Appendix I Tables 035 and 036; Segment 123 Element 237

protocolDomains.name: Acquirer
protocolDomains.sourceDescription: Accepts eCommerce transaction data from the merchant and passes it to Visa/MasterCard/Amex/Discover as applicable.

protocolDomains.name: Issuer
protocolDomains.sourceDescription: Determines whether authentication is available for the presented card account.

protocolDomains.name: Interoperability
protocolDomains.sourceDescription: Payment-network and software-provider infrastructure enables protocol operation between the Acquirer and Issuer domains.

protocolSteps: The cardholder enters card information on a merchant site using 3-D Secure to purchase goods.
The Merchant Plug-in contacts the Directory Server to initiate an authentication request.
The Directory Server routes the request to the appropriate Issuer Access Control Server.
The Directory Server sends the Issuer ACS response to the Merchant Plug-in.
The cardholder is directed to the Issuer's 3-D Secure browser page; the Issuer authenticates the cardholder using its chosen method, such as a password or one-time code.
The Issuer approves or declines the Authorization Request and returns an Authorization Response containing cryptographic data and applicable ECI/Terminal Type 25-29.
The cardholder is redirected to the merchant site and the purchase is completed.
sourceNotes: Appendix Y describes 3-D Secure as an identity-verification service intended to reduce eCommerce fraud; consult the 3-D Secure representative for further details.

Visa token-service merchants may optionally support TAVV together with 3DS CAVV; the source notes Visa support effective October 2018 and directs merchants to their First Data representative for availability. This is historical/program context, not a universal current activation rule.
The Visa scenario table says its usage examples are not exhaustive or all-encompassing.

Appendix I Table 036 identifies UCAF Security Level positions 1-2 as 21 or 24, position 3 as 0-7, Table Data length as 3 or 35, and a 32-character UCAF field when populated. It states that UCAF data is for MasterCard AAV, with subfield ID 43 and length 28; Identity Check values h and j are removed and must not be sent.

businessRequirements.title: The authorization response returns the applicable ECI/Terminal Type value 25, 26, 27, 28, or 29 and the Appendix Y brand mapping: Visa CAVV, MasterCard AAV, American Express AEVV.
Discover is named in the general 3-D Secure discussion, but Appendix Y does not specify a Discover cryptogram mapping; do not infer one from another brand.

For the three Visa scenarios in Appendix Y, use the stated CAVV/TAVV locations and applicability: Verified-by-Visa only uses Table 035; token only uses revised CAVV Element 195 with TAVV not applicable; combined Verified-by-Visa and Digital Wallet uses revised CAVV Element 195 and TAVV Element 237. The source says the matrix is not exhaustive.

Amex SafeKey Element 203 in Segment 123 consists of the SK indicator followed by a 28-character AEVV block and a 28-character AESK block; a non-applicable AEVV block and optional AESK block are space-filled. The SafeKey data blocks are base64 data.
American Express SafeKey is unavailable to OptBlue merchants; actual merchant program classification must come from authoritative enrollment evidence.

MasterCard AAV uses Segment 111 Table 036 UCAF Data; DSRP/token cryptogram uses Segment 123 Element 237. If both AAV and DSRP cryptograms are present, UCAF Security Level positions 1-2 must be 21. Table 036 security-level and subfield framing is bounded by Appendix I.
MasterCard SecureCode requires a 3-D Secure v1.0.2-or-better compliant MPI; the ATL105 message alone cannot establish implementation compliance.
The described 3-D Secure process spans the Acquirer, Issuer, and Interoperability domains and the seven Appendix Y process steps; actual system-to-system behavior needs external protocol evidence.
Brand/program availability and whether a merchant participates must not be inferred from the presence of message fields; confirm with the applicable representative or authoritative configuration.
Synthetic format checks do not prove that CAVV, TAVV, AAV, AEVV, or AESK is genuine, correctly generated, or accepted by a network/issuer; cryptographic validation requires trusted external evidence.

Appendix I states that Identity Check values h and j have been removed from MasterCard AAV and must not be sent; the precise data position/encoding is not safely inferred here, so payload-level validation remains review-required.

testCases.positive: ECI/Terminal Type 25-29 with the specified Visa, MasterCard, or Amex response cryptogram mapping
negative: cryptogram type does not match a named brand
Discover mapping asserted without an external authoritative definition

testCases.positive: Each of the three source-listed Visa cases uses its stated CAVV/TAVV element and length
negative: asserting the non-exhaustive matrix covers an unlisted Visa scenario

testCases.positive: Element 203 begins SK and has two 28-character base64 blocks, with only permitted blocks space-filled
negative: SafeKey submitted when authoritative merchant classification is OptBlue

testCases.positive: AAV framed in Table 036; DSRP cryptogram in Element 237; security level starts 21 when both are present
negative: combined cryptograms with a security level other than 21
Do not infer the field position/encoding for removed AAV values h and j

testCases.positive: Use separately sourced protocol, merchant enrollment, and cryptographic validation evidence
negative: claiming process flow, participation, availability, or cryptographic authenticity based only on a synthetic authorization payload

Appendix Y names Discover in general 3-D Secure discussion but omits its brand-to-cryptogram mapping.

Appendix I mentions Element 195 for Visa/Interlink tokenized transactions, but Appendix Y provides a Visa-specific matrix only; do not extend those rows to Interlink without authoritative confirmation.
Feature availability and merchant participation require confirmation from a representative or authoritative enrollment/configuration source.
The spec prohibits removed Identity Check values h and j but does not establish a payload position/encoding for a safe structural predicate.
Real protocol completion and cryptogram authenticity require trusted network/issuer/3-D Secure service evidence and cannot be synthesized.

testDataReadinessSummary.note: Synthetic fixtures exercise structural rules only. They do not establish cryptographic authenticity, actual 3-D Secure protocol completion, program availability, merchant enrollment, Interlink matrix behavior, or removed AAV value encoding.

testDataStatus: Appendix Y source material is represented across message-level mappings, Visa scenario rows, SafeKey format/eligibility, MasterCard UCAF/DSRP and MPI requirements, the three protocol domains and described process, plus explicit external-evidence boundaries. Unspecified Discover mapping and non-exhaustive scenario availability remain review-gated.
remaining: Obtain authoritative 3-D Secure process, merchant enrollment, and program availability evidence where behavior-level certification is required.
Obtain genuine network/issuer-approved cryptogram fixtures or a trusted validation contract before asserting cryptographic authenticity.
Confirm any Discover mapping and any Visa scenarios beyond the explicitly listed non-exhaustive matrix with the relevant representative.
Confirm Interlink 3-D Secure scenario applicability; Element 195's Interlink mention does not extend the Visa-only matrix.
Confirm the precise representation of removed MasterCard Identity Check AAV values h and j before adding a payload-level validator.
Keep appendix narrative and historical program availability distinct from message-level validation; do not derive enrollment from payloads.
